question: Does prior work already state the candidate minimum order six for a two-nonedge Braess set whose two singleton additions are non-Braess under the <= 0 convention, or explicitly give the E?zW witness and its exact sign pattern?

candidate.description: A diamond on vertices {1,2,5,6}, with pendant vertex 3 at 5 and pendant vertex 4 at 6.

evidence_inputs.role: sealed blind independent exact witness record
exact cross-evaluator agreement; final semantic gate remained separate

previously_reviewed_sources_reused: Sooyeong Kim's 2021 University of Manitoba thesis

fulltext_term_scan.interpretation_limit: Literal term absence supplements manual inspection and cannot establish absence of an equivalent result.

sources.citation: Yuxiang Hu and Steve Kirkland, Complete Multipartite Graphs and Braess Edges, Linear Algebra and its Applications 579 (2019), 284-301, DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2019.05.035.

locators.locator: PDF page 3, paragraph defining Braess and non-Braess edges
locators.finding: A Braess edge has strict positive change; a non-Braess edge is defined by change <= 0. The candidate's exactly zero f singleton therefore belongs to the published non-Braess side of the boundary.

Adding an edge to K_{8,8} is stated to have no effect on Kemeny's constant. Exact-zero edge additions were therefore already known; 'neutral edge' should be treated as descriptive wording rather than a new notion.
The paper gives another zero-change family boundary for complete split graphs and an explicit large integer example.

locators.locator: PDF pages 6-9, twin definition and Theorem 3.1.2
locators.finding: Nonadjacent vertices with the same neighborhood are twins, and Theorem 3.1.2 gives the exact Kemeny change after inserting their connecting edge for a general connected graph through quotient-chain stationary and hitting-time data.

candidate_relation.reason: In E?zW, N(1)=N(2)={5,6}; vertices 1 and 2 are nonadjacent twins of degree two. The same remains true after f=34 is added, so the theorem can analytically replay the sign of e before and after f once its quotient quantities are evaluated.
candidate_relation.reason_family_does_not_apply: The pendant vertices at 5 and 6 make the whole candidate neither a complete multipartite graph nor one of the complete split graphs classified in the paper.

sources.citation: Lorenzo Ciardo, The Braess' Paradox for Pendant Twins, Linear Algebra and its Applications 590 (2020), 304-316, DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2019.12.040; arXiv:1909.12549v1.

locators.finding: Every nontrivial connected graph becomes strictly twin-Braess when two new pendant twins at a common vertex are joined.
The paper points to Hu-Kirkland Theorem 3.1.2 for the distinct general formula concerning an edge between arbitrary nonadjacent twins.
In any connected graph of order at least four, joining existing pendant twins with a common neighbor strictly increases Kemeny's constant.

candidate_relation.reason: Vertices 3 and 4 are pendant but N(3)={5} and N(4)={6}; they are not pendant twins under the source's common-neighbor definition. The f=34 zero change does not contradict the strict pendant-twin theorem.
candidate_relation.reason_e: Vertices 1 and 2 are twins but are not pendant; the broader Hu-Kirkland formula is the applicable result.

sources.citation: Sooyeong Kim, Families of graphs with twin pendent paths and the Braess edge, Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra 38 (2022), 9-31, DOI 10.13001/ela.2022.5913; arXiv:2112.03655v1.

locators.locator: PDF pages 2-3, construction and definition of twin pendent paths
locators.finding: The two paths emanate from the same identified vertex, and the studied edge joins their pendant endpoints.

locators.locator: PDF page 6, Definition 3.6; PDF pages 7-8, Theorem 3.10
locators.finding: The paper defines the strict one-edge predicate and gives an exact sign criterion Phi_G(v,k1,k2)>0 for that construction.
Some parameter pairs make the auxiliary term phi_1 equal zero. This is not by itself a zero Kemeny change because the full criterion also contains phi_G, phi_2, and phi_3 terms.
The length-one/length-one common-root construction is always strictly Braess, restating the pendant-twin result.

candidate_relation.reason: The unique neighbors of candidate endpoints 3 and 4 are different, and they are not endpoints of two pendant path branches from one common cut vertex in the source's construction.

sources.citation: Nolan Faught, Mark Kempton, and Adam Knudson, A 1-Separation Formula for the Graph Kemeny Constant and Braess Edges, Journal of Mathematical Chemistry 60 (2022), 49-69; arXiv:2108.01061v1.
sources.review_status: previously reviewed; findings reused without counting against the three-new-paper cap

locators.finding: A Braess set is any set of nonedges whose joint insertion strictly raises Kemeny's constant. The definition does not require any proper subset, including singleton additions, to be non-Braess.

locators.locator: PDF page 10, paragraph immediately after Corollary 4.3
locators.finding: The P7 pair is a published two-edge example where neither singleton is Braess; it supplied the prior upper bound but was not claimed smallest.

sources.candidate_relation: The n=6 condition is a stricter, inclusion-minimal size-two Braess-set pattern under the <= 0 singleton convention. The general Braess-set notion and the existence of such singleton interaction are not new concepts.

source.citation: Ramin Javadi, Zeinab Maleki, and Behanz Omoomi, Local Clique Covering of Graphs, arXiv:1210.6965v1.
locators: arXiv HTML abstract paragraph abstract1.1 (local snapshot line 225)
arXiv HTML introduction paragraph S1.p2 and displayed definition S1.Ex1 (local snapshot lines 240 and 245)

namespace_mismatch_check.finding: The symbol rendered as kc(G) denotes the local clique cover number: the minimum per-vertex valency of a clique covering. It is unrelated to Kemeny's constant.
namespace_mismatch_check.bounded_implication: Any summary of this source that expands its kc(G) as Kemeny's constant is refuted by the primary text and illustrates a namespace collision. This source-side check does not score a retrieval system, because no raw retrieval output was audited here.

synthesis.convention: strict positive change is Braess; zero or negative change is non-Braess
synthesis.calibration: The last four false values mean only 'not located in this bounded review.' They do not establish global openness, first discovery, or publication novelty.

supported: By excluding every connected graph of orders two through five and exhibiting an order-six witness, the sealed two-evaluator exact finite census supports six as the candidate minimum order within the frozen connected simple undirected unweighted graph scope and <= 0 singleton convention, pending its designated final semantic gate; this is not a classification of larger graphs.
The six-vertex E?zW pair is smaller than the previously reviewed published P7 example.
The candidate combines one known-type twin edge with a second, non-twin neutral edge whose addition reverses the twin edge's sign.
requires_care: Call the result a candidate literature novelty or a new computationally located witness, not a new Braess-set concept.
Do not call exact-zero edges 'neutral Braess edges'; under Hu-Kirkland's definition they are non-Braess edges.
Do not infer total Kemeny neutrality from an auxiliary polynomial term being zero in Kim's criterion.
unsupported: first proof that the minimum is six in the literature
broad retrieval accuracy or failure rate from one namespace mismatch

useful_validation_shortcut.proposal: For a human-checkable one-instance derivation, apply Hu-Kirkland Theorem 3.1.2 to twin edge e=12 in both G and G+f, and independently derive the f=34 zero change from a standard exact Kemeny formula. This checks the sign reversal without repeating the full census.
useful_validation_shortcut.limit: The shortcut validates the witness only. It cannot prove the minimum; the exhaustive lower-order census remains necessary for that claim.

method_note: Primary full texts were retrieved and page-marked locally. The review used manual locator inspection plus a literal term scan. No graph enumeration or new Kemeny census was run.
